questions.question:
D3 — Issue 1: Make Save the visually primary action in the header?
Project/branch/task: main, /plan-design-review Pass 1 (Information Architecture) on the settings form plan.
ELI10: Right now Save, Reset, Cancel, and Export all look identical. A user scanning the header cannot tell which button finishes their task, and Reset and Cancel look just as inviting as Save even though they discard work. DESIGN.md already says Save is the only filled button and the other three are quiet ghost buttons.
Stakes if we pick wrong: users hesitate at the header or hit a destructive action by mistake; the page reads as assembled rather than designed.
Recommendation: 1A because it applies the exact existing DESIGN.md token, adds no new component, and fixes the hierarchy the plan itself flags. Principle: Hierarchy as service.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10, C=3/10
Net: apply the approved token now vs a weaker visual cue vs shipping four look-alike buttons.

options.label: 1A Filled primary Save (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Save becomes the one filled button (#1d4ed8, white text); Reset, Cancel, Export become neutral ghost buttons per DESIGN.md (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min)
✅ Reuses the existing Button component variants, so no new component or style family is introduced
❌ Ghost buttons must still be verified for visible boundaries and 44px targets at 320px

options.label: 1B Weight-only emphasis
options.description:
✅ Save gets bold text and a stronger border while all four stay ghost, a smaller visual change (human: ~30min / CC: ~5min)
✅ Keeps the header calmer if you feel a filled button is too loud
❌ Diverges from DESIGN.md's stated primary token, so the form will not match the rest of the app

options.label: 1C Leave as is
options.description:
✅ Zero implementation work and no visual change to review
✅ Avoids any risk of the filled button clashing with the persistent navigation
❌ Ships a header with no primary action; PLAN.md's own gap stays open and the pass stays at 6/10

questions.question:
D4 — Issue 2: Show the existing pending state while Save runs?
Project/branch/task: main, /plan-design-review Pass 2 (Interaction States) on the settings form plan.
ELI10: Saving takes 2 to 5 seconds and the proposed form gives no sign anything is happening. People assume the click did not register, click again, or leave before it finishes. DESIGN.md already defines the fix: a small spinner beside the word "Saving…" inside the disabled Save button, with the other three header actions disabled until it settles.
Stakes if we pick wrong: double submissions, users navigating away mid-save, and a page that feels broken exactly at the moment trust is decided.
Recommendation: 2A because it is the established DESIGN.md pending pattern, already used for Export, and it keeps the InlineStatus live region reserved for the outcome. Principle: Design for trust; edge cases are user experiences.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10, C=2/10
Net: reuse the existing in-button spinner vs a page-level skeleton that hides the user's edits vs shipping a frozen page.

options.label: 2A In-button Saving… spinner (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Save shows inline spinner + "Saving…", disabled, aria-busy=true; Reset/Cancel/Export disabled; all four re-enable on settle; reduced motion respected (human: ~1.5h / CC: ~10min)
✅ Same pattern Export already uses, so users learn one pending behavior, not two
❌ Spinner in a 44px button needs a reduced-motion fallback verified, not just a CSS class

options.label: 2B Full-form skeleton while saving
options.description:
✅ Very obvious that work is in progress; reuses the existing load skeleton (human: ~1h / CC: ~10min)
✅ Prevents any edits during the pending window by construction
❌ Hides the user's own values for up to 5s and repurposes a loading pattern for a submit, which DESIGN.md does not sanction

options.label: 2C Leave as is
options.description:
✅ No implementation work and no new behavior to test
✅ Avoids any motion on the page at all
❌ Users see a frozen page for 2-5s, PLAN.md's Motion gap stays open, and repeat submissions remain likely
